SoCO Research Workshop

# Bring the work before it’s finished.

The Research Workshop is a recurring multidisciplinary space for investigators to bring forward work in progress, challenge assumptions, refine methods, and develop collaborative projects across cutaneous oncology.

::: {.soco-actions}
[Upcoming workshop](#upcoming-workshop){.btn .btn-primary}
[Explore presentations](#presentations){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
[Journal Club](jc.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
:::

::::
:::::
::::::

::: {.soco-section .soco-forum-intro}

::: {.soco-eyebrow}
Why the Workshop exists
:::

## Good science gets better through criticism.

Many clinical investigators first receive sustained criticism only after a study has been designed, analyzed, and written.

The Research Workshop creates space to bring ideas forward **while there is still time to change them**—from an early clinical question or trial concept to preliminary analyses, methodological problems, and mature projects seeking broader multidisciplinary input.

The goal is not simply to present work. It is to make the work better.

:::

::: {.soco-section .soco-forum-principles}

::: {.soco-card-grid}

::: {.soco-card}
### Share early

Bring forward the question, design, or analysis before every consequential decision has been made.
:::

::: {.soco-card}
### Invite criticism

Make assumptions visible and give colleagues room to challenge the framing, methods, and interpretation.
:::

::: {.soco-card}
### Build together

Use discussion to identify collaborators, complementary expertise, and opportunities for multicenter science.
:::

:::

:::

::: {.soco-forum-callout}

::: {.soco-forum-callout-inner}

::: {.soco-eyebrow}
The working principle
:::

## Our best ideas deserve our colleagues’ best criticism.

Research Workshop sessions may include **new study concepts, trial designs, preliminary data, statistical or methodological questions, reproducibility challenges, data-sharing opportunities, and collaborative projects** across the spectrum of cutaneous oncology.

The work may be early. It may be incomplete. That is the point.

:::

:::

## October 28, 2026 {#upcoming-workshop}

Our next Research Workshop is a 90-minute, multi-stakeholder discussion built around cases, survey data, and open conversation.

:::

::: {.soco-proposed-meeting-card}

::: {.soco-proposed-meeting-kicker}
Research Workshop · October 28, 2026 · 3:30–5:00 PM ET
:::

### The Art of Authorship

**Who Gets on the Paper? Guidelines, Culture, and the Reality of Scientific Publishing**

A 90-minute, multi-stakeholder Research Workshop on how authorship decisions are actually made, why practice can diverge from established standards, and how investigators, editors, industry colleagues, and publication professionals may see the same problem differently.

::: {.soco-proposed-meeting-meta}
**Date:** October 28, 2026 · 3:30–5:00 PM ET  
**Format:** Case-based, moderator-led Research Workshop  
**Perspectives:** Academia · Editors · Industry · Publication professionals
:::

[View workshop →](https://societyofcutaneousoncology.org/research_forum/Art%20of%20Authorship/){.soco-card-link}

:::

::: {.soco-archive-heading}

::: {.soco-eyebrow}

## Future Workshops

### Inside the Review Room

**From Patient-Level Data to FDA Regulatory Decision-Making**

A 90-minute, moderator-led workshop exploring how oncology applications are reviewed inside FDA, how patient-level evidence is interrogated and reconstructed, and when advisory committees become part of the regulatory process.

::: {.soco-proposed-meeting-meta}
**Format:** Conversational, moderator-led workshop  
**Potential participants:** FDA regulatory medicine colleagues with a SoCO moderator
:::

[View meeting concept →](https://societyofcutaneousoncology.org/research_forum/inside%20the%20review%20room/){.soco-card-link}
